findings.evidence: PDF/Isospin.lean:16 ("for any two parton indices `u` and `d`"), :57-60, :124-132; `Species` has quark/antiquark constructors and no `map` (Particles/Parton/Species.lean:50-57, grep for `Species.map` finds nothing); `SumRuleAssumptions.momentum : ∀ Q2, (∑ i, mellinMoment f 1 i Q2) = 1` (PDF/Basic.lean:130); `chargeConj` is stated only for `Pdf (Species Flavor)` (PDF/ChargeConjugation.lean:71).
findings.fix: Say explicitly that `ι` is the quark-flavour index (the index of the `q_f + qbar_f` combinations `f2LO` consumes), not `Species Flavor`, and that on a species-indexed density the isospin involution is the species map induced by `Equiv.swap u d`, not a single swap. Either expose that species-level operation (the involution `quark i ↦ quark (swap u d i)`, `antiquark i ↦ antiquark (swap u d i)`, `gluon ↦ gluon`) and state `SumRuleAssumptions.isospinConj` against it, or drop the `SumRuleAssumptions`/`mellinMoment` transports here, since on the flavour index they have no sum rule to serve.
findings.issue: The module and definition docstrings advertise `isospinConj u d f = comap (Equiv.swap u d) f` as the neutron density "for any two parton indices `u` and `d`" (line 16; line 57-60 repeats it). For the repo's canonical parton index `Species Flavor` this is false: `isospinConj (.quark u) (.quark d)` swaps the quark densities and leaves `antiquark u`/`antiquark d` untouched, so the result is not the neutron. The exposed transport `SumRuleAssumptions.isospinConj` (line 124) effectively has no other intended index type — `SumRuleAssumptions.momentum` is `∑ i, mellinMoment f 1 i Q2 = 1`, a sum that equals 1 only over all species including the gluon (PDF/Basic.lean:129-133, cf. `chargeConj` which is stated only on `Pdf (Species Flavor)`). The exposed surface therefore invites a wrong instantiation under a name and docstring that assert it is the neutron.

summary: The isospinConj API is now complete and matches the chargeConj precedent, and f2LO_comap/f2LO_def close the unfolding gaps from the previous round. Remaining issue: isospinConj is documented as applying to "parton indices" and hence to Species-indexed densities, where a single Equiv.swap is not the isospin involution — and SumRuleAssumptions.isospinConj is exposed for exactly that index type.
